subject: Political Science
central_question: How have regional organisations and rising Asian economies emerged as alternative centres of political and economic power in the post-bipolar world?
in_scope_units: Overview: alternative centres of power after the end of bipolarity
European Union: post-war integration, institutions, influence and limits
Association of South East Asian Nations: origins, ASEAN Way, community pillars and regional role
The Rise of the Chinese Economy: command economy, gradual reforms, global integration and consequences
India–China Relations: historical background, border conflict, cooperation, trade and strategic tensions
Japan: economic, technological, diplomatic and security influence
South Korea: the Miracle on the Han River, human development and regional influence
banned_topics: A detailed history of US hegemony unrelated to the alternative centres discussed in this chapter
The full history of the Cold War and Soviet disintegration
A comprehensive history of SAARC beyond its limited use as a comparison in classroom activities

known_pitfalls.claim: The European Union is a single nation state with one foreign policy.
known_pitfalls.correction: The EU has supranational features, but member states retain separate foreign and defence policies in many areas.

known_pitfalls.claim: The ASEAN Way means adopting EU-style supranational institutions.
known_pitfalls.correction: It is informal, non-confrontationist and cooperative and places strong emphasis on sovereignty and non-interference.

known_pitfalls.claim: China used shock therapy to become a market economy.
known_pitfalls.correction: China opened its economy gradually, privatised step by step and retained a central role for the state.

known_pitfalls.claim: India–China relations are defined only by the 1962 conflict.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter also records decades of talks, trade growth, cultural and scientific cooperation, border-management measures and common positions in economic institutions.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Exercise 10 to reconstruct the sequence that produced the European Union.
Use NCERT Exercise 8 to explain the three pillars and objectives of the ASEAN Community.
Use NCERT Exercise 9 to compare China’s present economy with its earlier command economy.
Use NCERT Exercise 14 to organise contention and cooperation in India–China relations.
Use NCERT Exercise 13 to evaluate regional organisations as instruments of peace and prosperity.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The NCERT end-of-chapter Exercises contain Questions 1–14 covering chronology, MCQs, fill-in-the-blanks and analytical questions on the EU, ASEAN, China and India–China relations.
